category: Local runtime control plane for AI-assisted development.
promise: Run, inspect, and review parallel development workspaces without process, port, infrastructure, or browser-state collisions.
boundary: Agent-Up complements editors, coding agents, Git, Docker, and application frameworks; it does not replace them.
audience: Developers running and reviewing multiple agent-driven changes at once.
principles: Lead with the developer outcome, then explain the system.
Describe shipped behavior in the present tense and label Preview, Experimental, and Planned behavior explicitly.
Use concrete workspace language instead of generic AI superlatives.
Never imply that Desktop and Server automation share browser storage or navigation state.
Prefer direct verbs: run, inspect, review, restart, diagnose, and commit.

lifecycle.available: Shipped in the current public development-preview build.
lifecycle.preview: Usable, but its contract or experience may change.
lifecycle.experimental: Incomplete, opt-in, or not supported on every platform.
lifecycle.planned: Product direction only; not available to users.
